title: Two agents hand work back and forth for eleven days before anyone notices the bill
system: Four-agent LangChain pipeline (analyzer and verifier roles)
blast_radius: Reported USD 47,000 in model spend over eleven days. No data loss; the cost was the damage.
time_to_contain: the loop ran to the end of the billing cycle
summary: In a multi-agent pipeline, an analyzer and a verifier began returning work to each other rather than converging. Each hop was an individually reasonable decision — the verifier was not satisfied, so it sent the task back — and no component held a view of the run as a whole. There was no per-run spend ceiling and no step budget, so nothing in the system was in a position to notice. The loop was discovered from the invoice rather than from monitoring.
containment: Discovered post hoc from billing; the pipeline was subsequently given per-run budget ceilings.

sources.title: How to stop an AI agent from burning $47,000 in a loop nobody noticed

scenario.description: Two agents exchange a task indefinitely, each hop billing tokens, with no ceiling.
